# H2.6b — inline maps/sources, roots, URL lanes, and map faults: architecture and design packet

Status: **slice-opening design packet** for the H2.6b schedule row
([post-H1 schedule §4.5](../post-h1-completion-slices.md#45-maps-declarations-outputconfig-and-broad-qualification)):
inline maps/sources, `sourceRoot`, `mapRoot`, transformed/multi-source
ranges, source-map URL placement, and map failure behavior. This packet
authorizes **no production edit**. It freezes the pinned upstream owner
map for the H2.6b lanes, the current-Rust local-gap matrix at the
trusted base, the architecture-row dispositions, the H2.6b/H2.6c/H2.7d/
H2.7e boundary, the implementation ladder, and the W-H2.6B oracle
witness artifact. Each production packet in the ladder passes the
[mandatory design gate](../post-h1-completion-slices.md#11-mandatory-implementation-ready-design-gate)
in its own packet document before its first edit.

For semantics, vendored TypeScript 6.0.3 owns every fact; the current
code and tests plus [the current emitter architecture](../emitter-architecture.md)
own Rust structure. The H2.6a packet ([h2-6a.md](h2-6a.md)) is this
slice's parent: its §4 pinned the whole source-map subsystem, its
ladder landed the generator, the recording model, and the external
single-file lane, and its `boundary-controls` witness family froze the
oracle bytes for exactly the options this slice activates. This packet
re-derives every 6b-lane statement from the vendored bytes; nothing is
promoted from the 6a packet without re-validation at this trusted base.

## 4. Pinned upstream map (the H2.6b lanes)

The complete span+hash table is appendix §14. Every statement below was
read from the vendored bytes at the trusted base. The generator state
machine, recording sites, write order, and path planning are pinned by
the 6a packet §4 and are NOT restated; this section pins exactly the
lanes the 6a floor refused.

### 4.1 Option gates and conflicts (program-side, conformance-covered)

`verifyCompilerOptions` (124770-124777, 124855-124865): under
`inlineSourceMap`, both `sourceMap` and `mapRoot` are TS5053-class
conflicts ("cannot be specified with"); `inlineSources` and
`sourceRoot` each require `sourceMap || inlineSourceMap` (TS5051-class);
`mapRoot` requires `sourceMap || declarationMap` (TS5069-class). The
valid 6b option lattice is therefore: `{inlineSourceMap}` ±
`inlineSources` ± `sourceRoot`; `{sourceMap}` ± `sourceRoot` ±
`mapRoot` ± `inlineSources`. These diagnostics are validated by the
T0=100% conformance gate today and are NOT re-implemented; witnesses
assert the codes as observed context only.

### 4.2 Root lanes (`getSourceRoot` 116808-116811, `getSourceMapDirectory` 116812-116825)

- `getSourceRoot(mapOptions)` = `normalizeSlashes(sourceRoot || "")`,
  then `ensureTrailingDirectorySeparator` iff nonempty. The map's
  `sourceRoot` FIELD therefore carries the trailing-slash form of the
  option verbatim (`"src"` → `"src/"`; URLs pass through with a
  trailing `/`), and stays `""` (key still emitted) otherwise — the
  H2.6a-pinned serialization is unchanged.
- `getSourceMapDirectory(mapOptions, filePath, sourceFile)` — the
  `sourcesDirectoryPath` every `addSource` relativizes against:
  1. `sourceRoot` set → `host.getCommonSourceDirectory()` (the map's
     sources become common-directory-relative so the debugger resolves
     them under the declared root);
  2. else `mapRoot` set → `normalizeSlashes(mapRoot)`; with a source
     file, nest per-file: `getDirectoryPath(getSourceFilePathInNewDir(
     sourceFile.fileName, host, mapRoot))`; a RELATIVE result
     (`getRootLength === 0`) resolves against
     `host.getCommonSourceDirectory()`;
  3. else → `getDirectoryPath(normalizePath(jsFilePath))` (the H2.6a
     lane).
- The map FILE PATH is unaffected by roots: `getSourceMapFilePath`
  (116388-116390) stays `jsFilePath + ".map"` for
  `sourceMap && !inlineSourceMap` — `mapRoot` relocates the URL the
  consumer follows, never the written artifact.

### 4.3 URL lanes (`getSourceMappingURL` 116826-116857)

1. `inlineSourceMap` → `data:application/json;base64,` +
   `base64encode(sys, sourceMapGenerator.toString())`. NO
   `encodeURI` wraps the data URI. `sys.base64encode` (5007) =
   `Buffer.from(input).toString("base64")` — UTF-8 bytes, standard
   alphabet, padded; the `convertToBase64` fallback (17234-17254) is
   present but unreachable in the CLI (`sys` always provides the
   method). Rust: standard base64 over the UTF-8 map text.
2. else with `mapRoot`: `sourceMapDir = normalizeSlashes(mapRoot)`,
   per-file nesting as §4.2; if the result is RELATIVE it resolves
   against `getCommonSourceDirectory()` and the URL becomes
   `encodeURI(getRelativePathToDirectoryOrUrl(dirname(jsFilePath),
   combinePaths(sourceMapDir, mapFile), currentDirectory,
   canonicalFileName, /*isAbsolutePathAnUrl*/ true))` — a RELATIVE
   path from the JS to the expected map location (the `file://` arm
   applies on zero shared components); if the result is ROOTED the URL
   is `encodeURI(combinePaths(sourceMapDir, mapFile))` — an ABSOLUTE
   URL, not relativized.
3. else → `encodeURI(basename(sourceMapFilePath))` (the H2.6a lane).

`mapFile` in every external lane =
`getBaseFileName(normalizeSlashes(Debug.checkDefined(sourceMapFilePath)))`
— the checkDefined guard is unreachable-fatal for external lanes (the
path exists by 4.2's planning rule) and never runs in the inline lane.

### 4.4 Orchestration deltas (`printSourceFileOrBundle` 116744-116804, `emitJsFileOrBundle` 116587-116639)

Relative to the 6a-pinned sequence, the 6b lanes change exactly:

- generator construction passes `getSourceRoot(mapOptions)` and
  `getSourceMapDirectory(...)` (§4.2) instead of the `""`/js-dir floor;
- `sourceMapDataList` (→ `emitResult.sourceMaps`) is pushed for BOTH
  inline and external lanes, before the URL computation, exactly as 6a;
- the URL comment append (mid-line `rawWrite(newLine)` guard,
  `sourceMapUrlPos = writer.getTextPos()`, `writeComment("//# sourceMappingURL=" + url)`,
  no trailing newline) is IDENTICAL for both lanes — an inline-mapped
  file also ends without a final newline and also reports
  `sourceMapUrlPos` in the js write's `data`;
- the map write (`writeFile(..., sourceMapFilePath, toString(), false,
  sourceFiles)`) is gated on `sourceMapFilePath` — the inline lane
  writes NO map artifact, so the per-unit write order degenerates to
  the js write alone and `emittedFiles` (116633-116638) lists the js
  only;
- printer options carry `sourceMap`/`inlineSourceMap`/`inlineSources`
  (116611-116621); `sourceRoot`/`mapRoot` are orchestration-only and
  never reach the printer.

### 4.5 `sourcesContent` (`setSourceContent` 92421-92431, `setSourceMapSource` 121352-121370)

`setSourceMapSource` — already the live H2.6a registration point —
additionally calls
`sourceMapGenerator.setSourceContent(sourceMapSourceIndex,
sourceMapSource.text)` iff `printerOptions.inlineSources`. There is no
other caller. `setSourceContent(index, content)`: `content !== null`
guard (a null content is a complete no-op — no array allocation), then
null-pads `sourcesContent` to `index` and assigns. Serialization was
pinned at 6a §4.1: the `sourcesContent` key appears iff the array
exists, after `mappings`. Because registration happens at print start
for every printed file (6a §4.3), an `inlineSources` map carries the
full text of every registered source, including sources with zero
mappings. The dormant Rust port (`source_map.rs:140-150`, landed 6a
m-1) mirrors the null-pad/assign arms; m-1's gap row G4 verifies the
no-op arm byte-parity (upstream `content === null` vs Rust
`None`) before wiring.

### 4.6 Multi-source ranges: REACHABILITY FALSIFIED for the CLI

The printer's source-switch lane (`emitSourcePos` 121322-121332,
`sourceMapRange.source || sourceMapSource` at 121286/121288/121301,
`emitTokenWithSourceMap`'s `range.source` arm) activates only when a
node's `sourceMapRange.source` holds a FOREIGN `SourceMapSource`. At
this trusted base, `SourceMapSource` (17684-17688) has exactly two
other references in the whole of `_tsc.js`: the `objectAllocator`
export (`getSourceMapSourceConstructor`, 17697-17699 — the public-API
factory hook) and the printer consumption above. **No tsc-CLI code
path constructs one**: no transformer, no factory route, no emit
helper. `setSourceMapRange` (66 sites) only ever carries ranges whose
`source` is `undefined`. Therefore "transformed/multi-source
cross-file ranges" is unreachable through the compiler CLI, the
witness machine cannot produce a foreign-source case without
hand-driving the public API (prohibited: no hand-authored evidence),
and the Rust seam landed by 6a m-2 (source-switch save/restore with a
structurally-absent foreign source) is already upstream-exact. The row
closes as **upstream-parity-by-unreachability**; the public-API lane
(custom transformers constructing `SourceMapSource`) is owned by the
tsgo/public-API era, recorded in the deviations ledger via the m-2
packet. This is the same falsification class as 6a G12 (map-path
collisions).

### 4.7 Input source maps: dead-code closure

6a §4.2 pinned `appendSourceMap`/`decodeMappings`/`addName` as
tree-shaken dead in `_tsc.js` and delegated "H2.6b re-derives if its
packet proves reachability". This packet's §4.6 survey doubles as that
proof's negative: with no `SourceMapSource` construction and no
`appendSourceMap` caller, the input-source-map lane has NO tsc-CLI
entry point in 6.0.3. Disposition: typed-deferred to BLD1/L3 exactly
as the 6a table proposed; nothing to port, nothing to witness. The
6a-landed generator correctly omits these members.

### 4.8 Map sink faults (`writeFile` helper 16644-16655)

Every emit write funnels through the `writeFile` helper, which does NOT
try/catch: it passes an `onError` callback as the host `writeFile`'s
fourth argument, and ONLY a host that invokes
`onError(hostErrorMessage)` produces
`Diagnostics.Could_not_write_file_0_Colon_1` (**TS5033**, added to
`emitterDiagnostics` → `emitResult.diagnostics`); a throwing host would
propagate the exception out of emit entirely — the sanctioned fault
signal is the callback, never a throw. The map write precedes the js
write per unit (6a §4.4) and each write is an independent helper call,
so a failing MAP sink still attempts the js write — the observable
contract is: both writes attempted (both callback invocations occur),
one TS5033 per failing path, `emitSkipped` stays false. The W-H2.6B
`sink-fault` family observes this with a write callback that invokes
`onError` for exactly the `.js.map` path (and a control failing the
`.js` path). Rust models sink failures at the artifact loop; m-2's gap
row G7 aligns the map-arm behavior with the pinned per-write
independence and the TS5033 shape.

stays byte-identical); each packet's envelope names its own
allowed/forbidden paths.

1. **`h2-6b-m-1` — orchestration lanes (kind `foundation`).** In
   `crates/emitter/src/execute.rs` (+ a pure helper module if the
   packet so decides): generalize `source_map_recording_inputs` to the

| `map-root-shapes` | `mapRoot` relative (resolves against common directory; URL relativized from js dir incl. `..` climbs) vs rooted (absolute URL, `encodeURI` percent-escaping); per-file nesting with nested sources; map artifact still beside the js |
| `root-composition` | `sourceRoot`+`mapRoot` together under `sourceMap`; lowered es5 output through the live transform stack (composition facets) |
| `url-placement` | mid-line vs line-start URL append (missing final newline input), CRLF `newLine` under the inline lane, percent-encodable file names (data URI unaffected; external URL encoded) |

| `option-conflicts` | the §4.1 lattice as observed context: `inlineSourceMap`+`sourceMap`, `inlineSourceMap`+`mapRoot`, bare `inlineSources`, bare `sourceRoot`, `mapRoot` without a map option — expected codes asserted, emit behavior captured |
